description:
FILED s480 (Fable, 2026-09-09) from the s473f merge-review probes.  PRE-EXISTING in the sense that before s473f the whole SBCL backtrace was printed; #1247 (b) fixed the EXIT STATUS (probed: 2 / 3 / 255 / 2 / 7 / 255 / 255 / 0 / 255 for nine shapes, all = perl) and the hook prints perl's line, but the line is PRECEDED by SBCL's context.

PROBE (perl 5.40.3 vs `pcl`):
    open(my $f, "<", "/nonexistent/z"); die "boom\n";
    perl stderr:  boom
    pcl  stderr:  While evaluating the form starting at line 29, column 0
                    of #P"/tmp/pcl_316691_ihit.lisp":boom
    (rc 2 in both)

MECHANISM (measured, scratchpad deco.lisp): `sbcl --non-interactive --load FILE.lisp` -- SBCL's `load-as-source` wraps each top-level form's evaluation in a handler that PRINTS "While evaluating the form starting at line N, column M~%  of ~S:" to *error-output* and DECLINES; only then does `invoke-debugger` reach `sb-ext:*invoke-debugger-hook*` (the hook's own `(princ-to-string c)` is clean: `[boom]`).  Loading the COMPILED file (`--load FILE.fasl`) prints NO context.  So the hook cannot remove text that is already out, and the prefix is a property of running the emitted program as a SOURCE load.

WHO SEES IT: every uncaught die and every `Can't locate` from a failed require, on stderr, in every program run through `pcl` / `runpcl` -- and any harness that compares a child's stderr (fresh_perl_like on a dying child).  The sweep and companion did not move at s473f, so no registered row reads it today.

FIX SHAPES (pick by measurement): (a) a `handler-bind` at the program's outermost dynamic extent -- but the emitted file is a SEQUENCE of top-level forms (`(p-run-compile-phase-blocks)` then the statements), there is no single wrapper form, so this means either a per-top-level-form wrapper macro or a program-level entry that loads the body from INSIDE a handler-bind (a handler established inside the loaded extent runs before the loader's: handlers are innermost-first); (b) run the program from a compiled fasl -- the module cache already compiles modules; the PROGRAM is loaded as source, and #756's single-binary plan and the s473u transpile server both touch this seam; (c) SBCL-specific: bind `sb-ext:*evaluator-mode*`?  -- no: the message comes from load-as-source regardless of evaluator.  Do NOT strip the text in the hook (it is already printed).  Guard: `Pl/t/die-exit-status-01.t` gains a row asserting stderr == perl's stderr byte for byte for `die "boom\n"`.  SIZE: S-M; the design question is (a) vs (b).

=== RE-MEASURED s494 (Fable, Q5 failure-experience battery; ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s494/q5/) ===
Still open on main 863d3e20, and the shapes a USER meets: `pcl -e 'die "x\n"'` = 2 stderr lines (the context line + perl`s line; `-e` is never cached so it is ALWAYS a source load); a missing module under `pcl FILE.pl` = `While evaluating the form starting at line 27, column 0 of #P"~/.pcl-cache/scripts/<hash>.lisp":Can`t locate No/Such/Module.pm ...` (the script-cache .lisp is source-loaded on this path); `pcl -e 'my $o; $o->m'` = 32 lines (this context line + #2108(b)`s backtrace).  A file run from its cached FASL has no context line (first and second run of a fresh script both clean -- probed).
